problems.note: The unknown is now a width y on a can, so the question is in context and you must recognise that the width is a circumference. The formula and the radius of 3 stay the same.

steps.ask: The width wraps once around the can. Which length does that match, and which formula gives it?
steps.title: Use the circumference of the circle

lines.text: The width $\hl{1}{y}$ wraps once around the can, so it equals the circumference of the circle.

problems.note: This time the answer is an area, not a length, and the square's side is not given, so you first find the side from the circle (side = 2r).

steps.ask: Each side of the square just touches the circle. Which measurement of the circle is that side?
steps.title: Find the side of the smallest square around the circle

lines.text: The smallest four-sided figure that fits around a circle is a square with each side touching the circle, so its side is the diameter.

problems.note: The solid is now a cylinder, so the formula needs two lengths, r and h, instead of just r. The steps are the same: substitute, multiply, round.

steps.ask: What is the curved surface area of a cylinder, and which two measurements does it use?
steps.title: Find the curved area of 8 pipes

lines.text: The curved surface area of a cylinder is $2\pi \hl{2}{r} \hl{4}{h}$. There are 8 pipes with $\hl{2}{r = 1.65}$ and $\hl{4}{h = 23}$.

problems.note: The solid is now a cone, so the curved area uses the slant height l instead of the height h. It is worked in two steps: substitute, then evaluate and round.

steps.ask: What is the curved surface area of a cone, and which two lengths go into it?
steps.title: Substitute into the curved surface area formula

lines.text: Curved surface area of a cone is $\pi \hl{2}{r} \hl{4}{l}$, with $\hl{2}{r = 1.3}$ and $\hl{4}{l = 1.53}$.

lines.text: The diameter is twice the radius.

steps.ask: Which values from the question go into the standard equation for the centre and radius?
steps.title: Write the equation of a circle

lines.text: A circle with centre $\hl{1}{(h,k)}$ and radius $\hl{2}{r}$ has equation $(x-\hl{1}{h})^2+(y-\hl{1}{k})^2=\hl{2}{r^2}$. Here $\hl{1}{h=3}$, $\hl{1}{k=-4}$, $\hl{2}{r=7}$.

problems.note: The radius is now a surd, 4√2, so the right-hand side needs squaring: (4√2)² = 32. The centre and the method stay the same.

steps.ask: The radius is the distance from the centre to a point on the circle. Which formula gives a distance between two points?
steps.title: Find the radius

lines.text: The radius is the distance from the centre $\hl{1}{(-4, 3)}$ to the point $(3, 4)$.
